summary: Request for provable field-level redaction and cross-border provenance for SIEM streaming
description:
Issue summary: Nebula Bank requests a certified SIEM export pipeline that performs reversible pseudonymization for selected fields (PII), provides cryptographic provenance for cross-border deliveries, and an HSM-attested manifest proving retention windows and deletion timestamps.

Impact: Compliance team cannot complete an external audit without evidence that (1) field-level redactions are applied deterministically and can be mapped back by authorized custodians, (2) export manifests show chronological ordering and tamper-evidence across EU->US transfers, and (3) retention deletion events are captured and attested. This blocks contract sign-off for a payment-processing integration.

Environment: prod (eu-west primary), customer tenant nebula-bank-prod, SIEM sink: Nebula-managed Splunk HEC endpoint behind their MTLS proxy. Exports currently delivered via SFTP daily and via optional real-time webhook.

Requested deliverables:
- Sample exported batch for 2026-03-08 containing 10 anonymized events with mapping manifest and per-event HMACs.
- Documentation of field-level pseudonymization algorithm, rotation schedule for KEKs, and role required to reverse mapping.
- Signed manifest showing checksum chain (Ratcheted checkpoint) for cross-border transfer and RFC3161-style timestamps.
- Evidence that deletion requests submitted through API result in removal from next export within configured retention window, and proof of deletion recorded in audit ledger.

Attachments: customer supplied export schema (nebula_schema_v3.csv), example Splunk index mapping, and their legal cover letter (attached to ticket).
steps_to_reproduce: Customer provided sample payload and requested reproduction in staging using tenant nebula-staging
Support: replay 2026-03-08 slice through siem-exporter with pseudonymization enabled
Validate generated manifest and per-event HMACs against HSM-stored KEK (customer-importable verifying key)

comments: Customer (compliance@nebula-bank.com) 2026-03-10: 'We need an auditable proof that fields are pseudonymized in a reversible, auditable way for our auditors. Can Redwood provide an HSM-signed manifest and sample re-identification flow with RBAC gating.'

Support (Priya Patel) 2026-03-10: 'Acknowledged. We'll triage and validate sample export. Can you confirm whether reversal must be performed by Redwood or if Nebula will host the reversal key? Also confirming required retention proof format (RFC3161 or other).'

Customer 2026-03-10: 'Prefer Redwood attestation with an exportable verifying key. RFC3161 timestamps acceptable. We require KEK rotation schedule and proof that deleted records don't reappear in subsequent exports.'

SRE (Diego Martínez) 2026-03-11: 'I ran a staging replay and observed deterministic pseudonymization using tenant wrapping. Need product sign-off for exposing reversal API and documentation for key escrow flows.'

Eng (Anika Rao) 2026-03-12: 'Initial finding: current siem-exporter produces HMAC per event but does not emit a ratcheted checkpoint file suitable for cross-border chain-of-custody verification. One proposed fix: add signed checkpoint file and RFC3161 timestamping in export job. Sending PR for review.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Existing pseudonymization uses tenant-specific KEK which supports reversal by Redwood ops via KMS/HSM. Confirmed: HSM usage flagged in logs kek_id=kek-eu-17.
Hypothesis 2: Export manifest lacks ratcheting/checkpoint proof. Confirmed by inspecting sample batch: only per-event HMACs and a single batch signature exist; no incremental checkpoint chain.

Partial finding: Deletion API (DELETE /v1/audit/tenant/{id}/records) marks tombstone but tombstoned records are still present in raw backing store until retention sweep; exports do not currently filter tombstones unless run after sweep window.
Risk: If we provide reversal workflow, we must ensure RBAC gated workflow and audit trail; otherwise customer regulatory risk increases.
related_actions: Create engineering story to add ratcheted checkpoint manifest and RFC3161 timestamping (INT-4456)
Add export-time tombstone filter to siem-exporter for retention-compliant exports (INT-4470)
Schedule HSM attestation run and provide verifying public key bundle to customer (SEC-ops ticket)
resolution: Next steps defined: 1) Provide Nebula Bank a one-off sample export with HSM-signed batch manifest and 10 anonymized events by 2026-03-13 (workaround). 2) ENG to build ratcheted checkpoint + RFC3161 timestamping (story created). 3) SRE to enable export-time tombstone filtering for compliance exports. 4) Security to coordinate HSM attestation and supply verifying key. Customer notified of timeline and asked to confirm acceptance criteria for evidence pack.
follow_up_items: Confluence draft: siem-cross-border-playbook - add sample manifests and verifier snippets
Customer to sign NDA addendum for key escrow if they want Redwood-managed reversal
notes: Ticket holds regulatory urgency; coordinate with Legal for any key escrow conversations. Ensure any sample exports redact customer PII unless explicitly covered by signed NDA.
public_updates: 2026-03-11: Delivered one-off sample export with HSM-signed manifest to Nebula Bank. Awaiting confirmation of verifier acceptance.
